guide.summary: Dropbox documents OAuth 2.0 user authorization for individual accounts. Listing and continuation both use files.metadata.read through list_folder and list_folder/continue, so no content or write permission is required. Plan: register a web app, authorize one individual test account, then test listing and continuation with a read-only boundary check. App Folder root-path behavior and review or distribution requirements for other customer organizations remain unresolved.

steps.detail: Build the authorization URL with response_type=code, handle the redirect, and exchange the code for an access token. Do not run the flow yet.

evidence.quote: URL Structure https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize Note: This is the only step that requires an endpoint on www.dropbox.com . All other API requests are done via api.dropboxapi.com , content.dropboxapi.com , or notify.dropboxapi.com .
Method: GET Example: Auth URL for code flow
Example: code flow access token request
curl https://api.dropbox.com/oauth2/token \ -d code= < AUTHORIZATION_COD E > \
-d grant_type=authorization_code \ -d redirect_uri= < REDIRECT_UR I > \
-d client_id= < APP_KE Y > \

steps.title: Authorize one individual test account
steps.detail: Use a representative individual Dropbox test account with a sample App Folder. Complete consent, confirm the token response scope includes files.metadata.read, and confirm no team scope is requested. Boundary check: confirm the granted scope excludes content and write scopes.
steps.doneWhen: An access token is obtained for the individual test account and its granted scope includes files.metadata.read.

evidence.quote: In this flow: The user will be redirected to Dropbox to authorize your app to access their Dropbox data.
" scope " : " account_info.read files.content.read files.content.write files.metadata.read " ,

steps.title: Test metadata listing of the App Folder
steps.detail: Call list_folder with the test token and a folder path inside the App Folder. Replace the sample path with a real test folder; App Folder root-path behavior is not documented in the supplied sources. Expected response: entries with names and metadata, plus cursor and has_more. Boundary check: confirm entries contain only metadata and the request log shows only list_folder calls with no content download or write endpoints.
steps.doneWhen: Response returns entries for the test folder, and the request log shows only list_folder calls.

evidence.quote: curl -X POST https://api.dropboxapi.com/2/files/list_folder \

Response Successful response cursor string >=1 character

steps.doneWhen: Continuation runs until has_more is false, and the request log shows only listing calls.
